summary:
We have developed an interactive 3D educational website titled Abandoned but Not Forgotten, designed to bring the stories of historic space missions back to life. The project explores NASA's past Moon and Mars missions, featuring spacecraft, landers, rovers and scientific instruments that have completed their objectives and, in many cases, fallen silent.
Through an immersive 3D environment, interactive planetary maps, mission timelines, historical photographs, 3D visualizations, voice-assisted exploration and an interactive mission archive, users can discover where these machines went, what they accomplished and what they left behind.
The project addresses the challenge of preserving the legacy of missions that are often overlooked once their operations end. Their discoveries, scientific data and technological achievements laid the foundation for today's space exploration. By presenting their stories in an engaging and accessible format, we aim to ensure that even when these missions stop communicating, their contributions are never forgotten.
details:
1. ABOUT THE PROJECT

Our project, Abandoned but Not Forgotten, is an interactive website created to bring attention to space missions that have completed their journeys but are often forgotten over time.

We have brought together the stories of several NASA missions to the Moon and Mars, including Apollo, Surveyor, Viking, Spirit, Opportunity, Phoenix, InSight and Ingenuity. The website allows users to explore these missions, understand why they were launched, discover what they achieved and learn what happened to them after their missions ended.

2. WHAT WE DEVELOPED & HOW IT WORKS

Instead of presenting information through lengthy articles and static images, we wanted to make learning more interesting and engaging.

We developed an interactive 3D environment with features such as:

• 3D Planetary Exploration: Explore planetary surfaces through an interactive environment.

• Interactive Mission Maps: Locate and discover the sites of historic space missions.

• Mission Timelines: Follow the journeys and major milestones of different missions.

• Historical Photographs & 3D Visualizations: Get a closer look at spacecraft, rovers and their discoveries.

• Mission Comparisons & Quizzes: Compare missions and test your knowledge through interactive activities.

• ORBI – Virtual Space Companion: A virtual companion that guides users through the experience with voice-assisted interactions.

3. TECHNOLOGIES USED

The website was developed using:

• HTML

• CSS

• JavaScript

• 3D visualization and animation technologies.

4. FACTORS CONSIDERED BY OUR TEAM

While developing this project, our primary consideration was the accuracy and authenticity of information. We relied on information and resources from NASA's official website to ensure that mission details, discoveries and historical facts were presented reliably.

We also wanted to make the history of space exploration accessible to everyone, especially children and young learners. We wanted them to understand:

• How space research has progressed over the years.

• How earlier missions contributed to scientific discoveries.

• How those achievements paved the way for more advanced missions.

Another important consideration was storytelling. Rather than making the experience feel like reading a collection of historical articles, we decided to build a narrative around these missions, allowing users to follow their journeys and understand their stories. Our aim was to make learning engaging, interactive and enjoyable rather than overwhelming or boring.

5. BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT

What makes this project meaningful to us is the idea behind it. A mission ending does not mean its importance ends with it.

Many of the spacecraft and instruments featured on our website are no longer operational, but the data they collected and the discoveries they made helped pave the way for the space missions we know today.

Through this project, we hope to make these stories accessible to students and space enthusiasts while giving recognition to the missions that helped us take bigger steps in space exploration.

Our Aim is simple: Even if these machines have fallen silent, their contributions should never be forgotten.
